name: Italian Meatball Soup with Orzo, Kale & Lemon-Herb Toast (Two Ways)

ingredients.name: kale, cut and ready to use

instructions.primary_message: This recipe was created to feed two adults and two young children. You know your child (their tastes and appetite) best. Use this recipe as a template, adjusting ingredients, cooking methods, and portions as needed.
Preheat oven to 450°F. Coat a baking dish with a thin layer of oil.

Place pork sausage, Parmesan, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl. Using your hands, mix well to combine. Using a rounded tablespoon measure, form the pork mixture into meatballs and transfer to the baking dish. Place in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake until meatballs are golden and cooked through, about 15 minutes. Remove from oven.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 lb ground pork sausage
¼ cup Parmesan cheese, shredded
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, place broth and orzo in a medium saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Once simmering, reduce heat to medium-low and cook, stirring occasionally, until pasta is tender and liquid is mostly absorbed, about 10 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
chicken or vegetable broth
6 oz orzo pasta

instructions.primary_message: While the orzo is cooking, wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 stick celery
1 pint grape tomatoes
½ lemon

instructions.primary_message: Peel and trim carrots. Quarter 1 carrot lengthwise, then cut crosswise into 3-inch long sticks; place on a plate. Small dice remaining carrots and place in a medium bowl.
Trim and halve 1 stick of celery lengthwise, then cut crosswise into 3-inch long sticks. Add to the plate with the carrot. Small dice remaining celery and add to the bowl with the carrot.
Halve a ½-cup of tomatoes, add to the plate, and set aside for the kid plates. Add remaining whole tomatoes to the bowl.
Preheat another medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
While the pan heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion. Peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ medium yellow onion
1 clove garlic

instructions.primary_message: Once the pan is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggies and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are tender and tomatoes are starting to burst, 4-5 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tsp extra virgin olive oil
1 tsp Italian seasoning
½ tsp salt
¼ tsp crushed red pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, zest lemon into a small bowl. Peel and mince additional garlic. Add to the bowl with the lemon zest, along with oil and additional spices, then stir to combine the garlic-lemon oil. Cut lemon into wedges and set aside for serving.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 clove garlic
2 tsp extra virgin olive oil
¼ tsp parsley flakes
⅛ tsp salt
black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Spread garlic-lemon oil over two of the bread slices, then drizzle the remaining slice with plain olive oil. Arrange bread on a baking sheet pan. Add to the oven and bake until toasted 2-3 minutes; remove from oven and cut in half.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 slice sourdough bread
1 tsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.primary_message: Add 10 meatballs and 3/4 cup of orzo to the plate with the veggie sticks, then set aside.

Add remaining meatballs, orzo, and broth to the pan with the veggies, then gently stir to combine. Bring the soup to a boil, then add kale to the pan in handfuls, waiting for it to wilt slightly before adding the next handful. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until kale is tender, 1-2 minutes more. Remove from heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
chicken or vegetable broth
½ (10 oz) bag kale, cut and ready to use

instructions.primary_message:
FOR THE KID PLATES: Divide reserved meatballs, orzo, veggie sticks, and plain toast between plates. Top orzo with Parmesan. 

FOR THE ADULT PLATES: Divide soup between bowls, serve with garlic-lemon toast, and enjoy!
